angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 598,302 km at 171.03 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.8469 +/- 0.0111 mas (same row, RUWE 0.93): 171.03 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.86 +/- 0.05 solar radii from Turtelboom et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1246 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..293T/abstract): 598,302 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.87 +/- 0.03 solar masses from Turtelboom et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1246 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..293T/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5151 +/- 100 K from Turtelboom et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1246 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..293T/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Turtelboom et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1246 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..293T/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1246.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.509, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
